transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-10-31
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 44 minutes (calendar)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood PM) — Rajiv (CTO), Sofia (ML), Tom (PM), Elena (Security) — recorded on Fireflies

Summary:
Quick hands-on demo: JSON sandbox and action-contracts, show guardrails, fallback patterns, hosted vs dedicated latency trade-offs, and pilot scope. Customer wants to validate private deployment patterns and run latency-sensitive generation for search re-rank use-case.

Topics covered:
- JSON-mode and strict schema enforcement
- Tool/function calling patterns & safety guards
- Runtime fallbacks and canary rollouts
- V P C / on-prem options, K M S / key mgmt, audit logs
- Benchmarks and pilot scope

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right hey everyone thanks for joining on a Saturday afternoon, um we appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:04] Rajiv Menon: Hey Rajiv here.
[00:06] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, hi.
[00:07] Tom Becker: Tom.
[00:08] Elena Wu: Elena from security.
[00:09] Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood SE.
[00:10] Maya Patel: Great ok, super. Today we'll walk through the JSON sandbox, action contracts, show a couple of runtime fallbacks and then discuss pilot next steps. we'll try to keep it hands-on.
[00:22] Tom Becker: Quick ask — we're mostly interested in the re-rank flow that sits behind search, so short inputs, high QPS, tight 95p latency budget.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Perfect that helps frame it. so we can show continuous batching and KV caching but also how to maintain 95p latency under X QPS.
[00:38] Sofia Alvarez: curious — in your demo can you show a sample schema for the output? we need strict JSON so downstream systems don't break.
[00:45] Liam Chen: Yep we'll flip to the sandbox. we have two modes — permissive json and strict schema mode. in strict mode the runtime validates the LLM output against a typed contract and if it doesn't match it triggers a fallback: either re-ask with a stronger system prompt or route to a simpler deterministic tool.
[01:02] Rajiv Menon: When you say tool, do you mean internal functions or external webhooks? we have some downstream microservices that expect a POST.
[01:08] Liam Chen: Both. our function-calling supports typed arguments and you can map calls to in-cluster services or external endpoints. there's also a sandboxed executor when you want isolated tool runs.
[01:17] Elena Wu: security question — how do you handle keys for external services, K-M-S, H S M etc? we can't expose secrets in logs.
[01:24] Maya Patel: Good question. we integrate with customer K M S — redwood never persists raw secrets; there is envelope encryption and audit logging. logs can be redacted and we support customer-managed keys for private deployments.
[01:36] Elena Wu: and SOC two?
[01:38] Rina Kapoor: We're SOC2 Type II compliant, we can share the report and a controls mapping. i'll attach that to the notes.
[01:45] Sofia Alvarez: nice. okay demo when you're ready.
[01:47] Liam Chen: switching share to the sandbox — bear with me, screen share lag. so here's the JSON sandbox URL, quick link we shared earlier: https://redwood-internal/sandbox/zenarc-demo (note: ephemeral)
[02:05] Liam Chen: first example — re-rank contract. schema: top-level object with items: array of {id: string, score: number, rationale: string}. i will show how the runtime enforces that score is numeric and between 0 and 1. if the model spits text we'll coerce in permissive mode or reject in strict mode.
[02:28] (typing noises)
[02:33] Sofia Alvarez: are you using a separate model for rerank vs generation, like a small reranker?
[02:37] Liam Chen: good catch — you can pin different models per route. many customers run a smaller dense-re-ranker on Dedicated capacity then a larger generator for long-form. for re-rank we usually recommend a quantized 7B variant for throughput unless you need high-precision semantics.
[02:55] Rajiv Menon: what's the unit cost implication? if we run high QPS re-rank on dedicated, is it better than hosted?
[03:02] Maya Patel: Dedicated tends to be more predictable on unit cost at scale because you're reserving capacity. Hosted is simpler to start and you get auto-scaling, but unit cost can be higher for sustained throughput. our Optimize tool suggests batching + quantization profiles to hit your cost target.
[03:20] Tom Becker: Can you demo a guarded tool call? show the fallback to a deterministic service if schema validation fails.
[03:25] Liam Chen: yes — pipeline: model -> schema validator -> if fail -> re-prompt w/ stronger instructions -> if still fail -> call deterministic scorer tool. i'll run it now.
[03:40] [screen: request payload posted]
[03:43] Liam Chen: sending prompt set 'zenarc_re_rank_examples_v1' — watch for a forced malformed response to trigger fallback.
[03:51] [silent for typing]
[03:59] Liam Chen: model returned free-form text, schema rejected — runtime logged the failure and re-issued a constrained prompt with explicit typed output. second attempt succeeded and we returned a typed array. you can see the audit trail in the console with request_id and the validation errors.
[04:20] Sofia Alvarez: is the audit trail retained? we have retention policies for two years for compliance.
[04:26] Maya Patel: retention is configurable for Private and Dedicated; Hosted has tiers for retention. for Private (V P C) customers you can set long-term retention in your storage or push logs to your S I E M.
[04:40] Elena Wu: can we redact P I I from logs automatically?
[04:43] Liam Chen: yes redaction hooks are configurable; you can supply regex or structured redaction rules.
[04:49] Rajiv Menon: on latency — show a live trace for a request and break down where time is spent.
[04:54] Liam Chen: sure. here's a trace — tokenization 5ms, KV cache lookup 8ms, model decoding 60ms, postprocessing + validation 12ms. with batching at 8 requests the per-token time rises slightly but cost drops.
[05:15] Tom Becker: what's KV cache again? we've heard K V cash earlier in docs and it was confusing.
[05:20] Liam Chen: it's the key-value cache for transformer decoder states — it speeds up multi-turn and re-use of prefixes. some transcripts autogen messes it up — K V cash.
[05:27] [laughter]
[05:30] Sofia Alvarez: haha okay. can we force a canary rollout? say we want 10% traffic to new quantized model and fallback to old model if errors spike.
[05:37] Rina Kapoor: short answer yes — rollout policy supports percent-based, metric-based with auto-fallback, and A/B. you can wire the console to monitor failures and automatically rollback.
[05:48] Rajiv Menon: network topology — if we go Private in our V P C, will traffic egress hit our NAT? how are connections established?
[05:55] Maya Patel: for Private deployments we either run an agent in your V P C or an on-prem cluster that talks to the control plane over a customer-owned connection. egress is configurable and you can set up private peering. we can share the network diagram — i'll attach it.
[06:10] Elena Wu: need details on ingress filtering and allowed IPs for our infra team.
[06:14] Maya Patel: we'll get that to you.
[06:16] Tom Becker: question about safety: if the model calls a tool that executes code, how do we ensure the tool can't exfiltrate data?
[06:23] Liam Chen: sandboxed executor runs with least-privilege and you can configure access control lists for each tool. plus we support dry-run mode where calls are logged but not executed.
[06:32] Sofia Alvarez: can the runtime transform outputs before hitting tool endpoints? e.g., strip P I I and map fields?
[06:38] Liam Chen: yes transformation hooks are supported. you can run a rewrite step that uses a safe template or a deterministic mapper.
[06:45] [pause — small conversation between Rajiv and Tom off-mic]
[06:58] Lily: (mis-attributed) sorry ignore —
[07:02] Maya Patel: let's pivot to pilot scope. we propose a 2-week pilot: week one — sandbox integration + benchmark; week two — pilot on Dedicated with limited traffic and monitoring; objective: validate 95p latency at target QPS and measure unit cost.
[07:18] Rajiv Menon: what telemetry do we get? we need token-level cost, per-route latencies, and per-request schema validation failures.
[07:25] Liam Chen: console gives token-level cost, breakdown by model and route, validation error rates and downloadable traces. we'll share an example dashboard link.
[07:36] Sofia Alvarez: will you simulate load? we want synthetic spikes and some outlier runs.
[07:40] Liam Chen: yes Liam will run a synthetic harness from multiple regions to simulate tail latency.
[07:44] Tom Becker: pricing — how do you bill for retries and validation re-asks?
[07:49] Maya Patel: retries count as additional tokens; our billing reflects consumed tokens across all attempts. in pilots we often discount or provide credits so you can validate without large spend.
[07:59] Rajiv Menon: can we set a hard cap to avoid surprise bills?
[08:02] Maya Patel: yes quotas and alerts — we also offer soft limits on Hosted. Dedicated is contract-based.
[08:10] Elena Wu: will you support S S O (SAML) and RBAC?
[08:14] Rina Kapoor: yes S S O, SCIM user provisioning, and role-based controls are supported; we'll send the admin guide.
[08:20] Sofia Alvarez: two last things — can we run the re-rank flow with a local model in our datacenter in the pilot?
[08:26] Liam Chen: for Private we can register your local model endpoint and Redwood routes to it — that'll be similar to on-prem. it's more setup but doable for the pilot if you have infra capacity.
[08:36] Rajiv Menon: what's the expected lead time for Private deployment?
[08:39] Maya Patel: typically 3–6 weeks depending on procurement and networking; Dedicated can be faster if you take a reserved pool.
[08:47] Tom Becker: procurement has to review contracts — can legal get the standard terms?
[08:50] Maya Patel: yes i'll attach the S L A and standard terms.
[08:54] Elena Wu: please include data residency and data processing addendum.
[08:58] Maya Patel: will do.
[09:00] [wrap-up]
[09:02] Maya Patel: recap: we'll send pilot proposal and pricing, run benchmark with your prompt set, share SOC2 + K M S note and network diagram, and schedule kickoff. any other open items?
[09:12] Sofia Alvarez: send sample code for the typed tool contract.
[09:15] Liam Chen: i'll upload an example repo and the typed schema templates.
[09:19] Rajiv Menon: thanks — this was helpful.
[09:22] Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll follow up in email.
[09:24] (call ends)
